assessment.headline: AI demand still strong, but credit stress and grid bottlenecks are building around the buildout.
assessment.digest_markdown:
**What changed this week**

The official data still shows an AI spending boom. Hyperscaler capex rose 22% quarter on quarter in Q2. Taiwan's AI-server suppliers grew a median 77% year on year in September. Signed-but-not-started data-center leases jumped 52%.

The warning signs are coming from **how the boom is financed and built**, not from demand:

- **Credit:** Oracle's default-insurance cost hit an 18-year high after a downgrade to the lowest investment-grade rung. Big-tech bond spreads have widened and order books have thinned. High-yield spreads rose 0.4 points in four weeks. Alphabet, Amazon and Oracle all had negative free cash flow last quarter, so they increasingly depend on debt and stock sales.
- **Physical limits:** PJM, the largest US grid operator, reports about 4 GW of data-center load canceled or delayed. Texas has effectively paused new approvals. Oracle's Project Jupiter is under a force majeure notice.
- **OpenAI:** Its revenue run-rate was clarified at about $50B rather than $68B. AI stocks fell 3–8%, showing how fragile sentiment is.

**Why it matters**

If money gets more expensive (the 10-year Treasury yield is at 5.22% and Brent oil at $125) or power can't be delivered, capex could slow even while demand stays strong. On the positive side, GPU rental prices are rising and suppliers report more demand than they can ship.

**What to watch**

Meta reports Oct 21, Microsoft and Alphabet Oct 28, and Amazon Oct 29. Look for changes to capex guidance and words like "pacing" or "digestion." Also watch Oracle's credit spreads and any pulled bond deals.

*Not investment advice.*

Microsoft and Alphabet earnings Oct 28 and Amazon Oct 29: capex guidance, free cash flow and any 'pacing'/'digestion' language
Oracle 5-year CDS and bond prices; any pulled or downsized hyperscaler or data-center debt deals
Taiwan October monthly revenue (around Nov 10), the first month of the deceleration check
PJM cancellation updates and how long the Texas approval pause lasts

amounts.sentence: As of June 30, 2026, we had additional leases, primarily for datacenters, that had not yet commenced of $ 329.1 billion, with some arrangements subject to certain contractual conditions being met.
As of June 30, 2026, we have entered into leases, primarily related to data centers, that have not yet commenced with future lease payments of $ 85.2 billion that are not yet recorded.

These lease obligations were approximately $278.99 billion, consisting of data centers, colocations, and certain network infrastructure, which will commence during the remainder of 2026 through 2036 with lease terms ranging from greater than one year to 30 years.
In July 2026, we entered into additional data center leases with lease obligations of approximately $68 billion, which are expected to commence in 2027 and 2028, with lease terms of 18 to 20 years.

MSFT.name: Microsoft
MSFT.summary: The release gives no capex guidance; it says forward-looking guidance will come on the earnings call, and its risk factors mention substantial cloud and AI investments, the risk of being unable to expand adequate infrastructure, and possible capacity constraints.

GOOGL.name: Alphabet
GOOGL.summary: The release contains no capex guidance; it cites strong demand for AI infrastructure and AI solutions driving 82% Google Cloud growth, and says net proceeds of $49.6 billion from June 2026 stock issuances will be used for general corporate purposes, including capital expenditures to scale AI infrastructure and global compute.

AMZN.name: Amazon
AMZN.summary: The release gives no forward capital-expenditure guidance; it reports that trailing-twelve-month free cash flow turned to an outflow of $7.6 billion, driven primarily by a year-over-year increase of $66.1 billion in purchases of property and equipment, which primarily reflects investments in artificial intelligence.

META.name: Meta
META.summary: Meta expects 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, of $130-145 billion, narrowed from its prior outlook of $125-145 billion; second-quarter capital expenditures were $31.08 billion.

guidance.sentence: We anticipate 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, to be in the range of $130-145 billion, narrowed from our prior outlook of $125-145 billion.

ORCL.name: Oracle
ORCL.summary: The release gives no capital-expenditure guidance figure; it says AI cloud demand continues to outpace supply, with 850MW of additional datacenter capacity and more than 300,000 GPUs delivered, RPO rising to $664 billion, negative free cash flow of $5 billion due to Cloud Infrastructure investments, and $20 billion of common stock sold under its capital investment program.
